sections.title: NERN TX TO LOWER MS VALLEY...WRN TN VALLEY AND SWRN OH VALLEY
sections.text: CONSOLIDATED QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY EXTENDS FROM SRN INDIANA SWWD THROUGH SERN MO TO A SURFACE MESO-LOW IN WRN AR. COLD FRONT STRETCHES SWWD FROM THE LOW INTO NERN...SCNTRL AND SWRN TX NEAR DEL RIO. A MOIST WARM SECTOR WITH MID-UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS HAS ADVECTED THROUGH ERN TX INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY. THE MESO-LOW WILL DEVELOP NEWD ALONG THE FRONT FROM SWRN AR INTO THE OH VALLEY IN RESPONSE TO AGEOSTROPHIC FORCING ATTENDING AN UPPER JET LIFTING NEWD THROUGH POST FRONTAL ZONE. THIS PROCESS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO ACCELERATION OF THE COLD FRONT THROUGH ERN TX INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY OVERNIGHT. THE 00Z RAOBS FROM LITTLE ROCK AND SHREVEPORT INDICATE MORE INSTABILITY THAN SHOWN ON THE OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS WITH 1000 J/KG MLCAPE WHEN CORRECTED FOR WET BULB EFFECTS BETWEEN 600-700 MB. STORMS WILL LIKELY TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING ALONG CONSOLIDATED BOUNDARY FROM NERN TX...SWRN AR INTO SRN IND...WITH ZONE OF DEVELOPMENT GRADUALLY SHIFTING EWD WITH TIME. OTHER CONVECTION IS ALSO FORMING OVER ERN AR WITHIN ZONE OF WARM ADVECTION JUST AHEAD OF THE FRONT. GREATEST TORNADO THREAT IS EXPECTED ACROSS CNTRL THROUGH ERN AR THIS EVENING /ESPECIALLY NE OF THE MESOLOW/ AS STORMS TRAIN NEWD ALONG

sections.title: SERN TX THROUGH SRN LA
sections.text: FARTHER SOUTH FROM ERN TX INTO LA...OTHER STORMS WILL CONTINUE DEVELOPING ALONG THE COLD FRONT AS IT INTERACTS WITH MOIST AXIS. TENDENCY WILL BE FOR THESE STORMS TO BE UNDERCUT AS THE FRONT SURGES SEWD...WHICH MAY LOWER OVERALL SEVERE POTENTIAL. NEVERTHELESS...SOME THREAT WILL EXIST FOR ISOLATED STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO. MODELS SUGGEST A FEW STORMS COULD DEVELOP IN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR FROM SERN TX INTO SRN LA. IF THIS OCCURS THEN SEVERE THREAT COULD BE GREATER THAN CURRENTLY INDICATED. GIVEN TENDENCY FOR DEEPER FORCING TO SHIFT AWAY FROM THE GULF COASTAL REGION...CONFIDENCE IN ROBUST WARM SECTOR INITIATION IS NOT PARTICULARLY HIGH AT THIS TIME. ..DIAL.. 01/13/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE DEVELOPMENT AND/OR TRANSITION TO SURFACE-BASED STORMS IS EXPECTED TO BEGIN OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. ONCE THIS BECOMES APPARENT...A TORNADO WATCH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED TO ADDRESS AN INCREASING THREAT FOR DMGG WINDS AND ISOLD TORNADOES BY THE LATE AFTERNOON THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 19Z SURFACE MESOANALYSIS SHOWS A 1005 MB SURFACE LOW 30 MI E DAL AND A COLD FRONT DRAPED SW TO NE FROM NEAR THE DFW METROPLEX THROUGH W-CNTRL AR AND INTO SERN MO. THE SRN PORTION OF THE FRONT WILL ACCELERATE EWD INTO FAR NERN TX BY EARLY EVENING AS THE LOW DEVELOPS NEWD...BUT THE PORTION OF THE FRONT OVER AR IS EXPECTED TO MOVE LITTLE OR SLIGHTLY NWD OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. AS SUCH...LOW LEVEL MOISTURE /MID-UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS/ LEADING TO A DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE NWD INVOF THE FRONT OVER CNTRL-NERN AR. DESPITE A THICK MID-HIGH LEVEL CLOUD CANOPY RETARDING SURFACE HEATING...TEMPS ARE GRADUALLY WARMING INTO THE LOW 70S OVER THE ARKLATEX REGION. THIS HAS CONTRIBUTED TO UPWARDS OF 1500 J/KG MLCAPE WHEN MODIFYING THE 12Z SHV RAOB --FEATURING A 14-15 G/KG MEAN MIXING RATIO-- FOR THE 19Z TXK SURFACE OBSERVATION. MOIST LOW LEVELS COMBINED WITH A STRENGTHENING LLJ TO 55 KTS BY 00Z...WILL ENLARGE HODOGRAPHS /500 M2/S2 0-1 KM SRH/ AND FACILITATE AT LEAST THE POTENTIAL FOR DMGG WINDS AND ISOLD TORNADOES WITH A MESSY CONVECTIVE MODE FOCUSED NEAR THE FRONT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CORRIDOR OF TORNADIC POTENTIAL EXISTS FROM SWRN AR ACROSS CNTRL AND EVENTUALLY NERN AR THROUGH THE EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS CONTINUE TO TRAIN FROM NERN TX ACROSS SWRN AR AND INTO NRN AR...MAINLY ALONG AND N OF THE SYNOPTIC BOUNDARIES. STORMS OVER SWRN AR ARE CURRENTLY SITUATED NEAR THE SURFACE LOW...WHICH WILL TRANSLATE NEWD ALONG THE SYNOPTIC WARM FRONT THIS EVENING. THIS WILL BE THE MOST LIKELY CORRIDOR FOR A FEW TORNADOES. THE 00Z LZK SOUNDING IS IMPRESSIVE AND INDICATES MORE INSTABILITY THAN RAP-BASED OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS FIELDS INDICATE. EVEN CONSERVATIVELY INCREASING THE MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES AND DECREASING THE SURFACE DEWPOINT TO 65 F STILL YIELDS AROUND 1000 J/KG MUCAPE...AT LEAST QUADRUPLE WHAT THE RAP MODEL WOULD INDICATE. SHEAR PROFILES REMAIN VERY STRONG...WITH PARAMETERS FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS AND TORNADOES. EFFECTIVE SRH IS OVER 500 M2/S2. CELLS OVER SWRN AR CURRENTLY SHOW ROTATION. THESE STORMS SHOULD MOVE ROUGHLY ALONG THE FRONT AND WITH THE SURFACE LOW. ANY DEVIANT MOTION JUST A BIT TO THE RIGHT MAY GREATLY ENHANCE TORNADO POTENTIAL. IF THE COLD FRONT UNDERCUTS TOO QUICKLY...TORNADO POTENTIAL WOULD BE GREATLY REDUCED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A THREAT OF SEVERE WIND GUSTS AND A BRIEF TORNADO REMAINS...BUT THE OVERALL THREAT APPEARS TO BE DECREASING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR TRENDS HAVE SHOWN A DECREASE IN ROTATION SIGNATURES ACROSS CNTRL AND SWRN AR AS WIND PROFILES INDICATE SOME VEERING. HOWEVER...SOME BOWING STRUCTURES ARE EVIDENT OVER SWRN AR AS THE COLD FRONT ACCELERATES EWD. AS SUCH...IT APPEARS THAT THE TORNADO THREAT MAY BE TRANSITIONING TO MORE OF A DAMAGING STRAIGHT LINE WIND THREAT. HOWEVER...EMBEDDED CIRCULATIONS MAY STILL OCCUR DUE TO STRONG LOW LEVEL SHEAR WITH A MARGINAL TORNADO THREAT. A RELATIVELY MOIST AND MARGINALLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS REMAINS AHEAD OF THE FRONT...FROM ERN TX NEWD TO THE OH RIVER. THIS MAY CONTINUE TO FUEL STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS. HOWEVER...UNLESS AN OVERALL INCREASE IS NOTED...AN ADDITIONAL WW MAY NOT BE NEEDED. ..JEWELL.. 01/13/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTION IS GROWING IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY OVER PREFRONTAL WARM SECTOR IN E TX. GIVEN STRENGTH OF AMBIENT WIND FIELDS AND SHEAR PROFILES...ANY SUSTAINED WARM-SECTOR CONVECTION MAY OFFER RISK OF DAMAGING GUSTS AND A FEW TORNADOES...WHETHER FROM SUPERCELLS OR CIRCULATIONS EMBEDDED IN QUASI-LINEAR SEGMENTS. ADDITIONAL WW MAY BE REQUIRED IF CURRENT INCREASING TRENDS CONTINUE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWS SOMEWHAT WAVY ARCTIC COLD FRONT FROM NERN AR SWWD THROUGH LIT AREA TO CADDO PARISH LA...BASICALLY BISECTING WW 3...THEN SWWD ACROSS PANOLA AND HOUSTON COUNTIES TX TO MIDDLE TX COASTAL PLAIN. FRONT WILL PROCEED SEWD ACROSS MOST OF DISCUSSION AREA THROUGH 09Z. THIS BOUNDARY IS SHARPLY DEFINED AND STG...UNDERCUTTING CONVECTION DEVELOPING ALONG OR IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF IT. THIS PROCESS SHOULD QUICKLY HALT SVR WIND AND TORNADO POTENTIAL WITH SUCH ACTIVITY. HOWEVER...MODIFIED SHV/LCH RAOBS SUGGEST MINIMAL MLCINH OVER WARM SECTOR IN EXTREME E TX AND LA...ALONG WITH 500-1000 J/KG MLCAPE. LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE TRANSPORT AND WAA SHOULD OFFSET/RESTRICT PACE OF DIABATIC SFC COOLING ENOUGH TO KEEP EFFECTIVE LIFTED PARCELS ROOTED AT OR VERY NEAR SFC FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS. LLJ MAY DIMINISH WITH TIME AFTER 06Z...BUT STILL SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO ENLARGED HODOGRAPHS THROUGH MOST OF PRE-DAWN HOURS. AS SUCH...SLY-SSELY SFC WINDS BENEATH LLJ SHOULD RENDER EFFECTIVE SRH VALUES 250-500 J/KG OVER MUCH OF THIS AREA...WITH ONLY GRADUAL SFC VEERING EXPECTED OVERNIGHT. MEANWHILE...DEEP-LAYER SHEAR SHOULD REMAIN FAVORABLE FOR ORGANIZED SVR...E.G. EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES 55-65 KT OVER MOST OF PREFRONTAL AIR MASS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS WILL AFFECT THE REGION WITH LOCALLY SEVERE WINDS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A STRONGLY FORCED LINE OF THUNDERSTORMS NOW ALONG THE IL/INDIANA BORDER WILL AFFECT MUCH OF SRN IND AND NRN KY ALONG THE OH RIVER OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS...AND MAY PERSIST INTO SWRN OH. SURFACE ANALYSIS INDICATES MODERATE PRESSURE FALLS AHEAD OF THIS EVOLVING FEATURE...WHERE STRONG WARM ADVECTION WAS OCCURRING DUE TO A 50+ KT LOW LEVEL JET. MARGINAL INSTABILITY HAS DEVELOPED AS THE WARM FRONT LIFTS NWD...WITH MUCAPE ON THE ORDER OF 100-300 J/KG INTO SRN IND AND SWRN OH. ALTHOUGH SHEAR IS VERY STRONG...WIDESPREAD SEVERE IS UNLIKELY DUE TO VERY POOR LAPSE RATE PROFILES. HOWEVER...MECHANICAL MIXING MAY RESULT IN LOCALLY SEVERE WINDS AS THIS LINE PASSES...AND THIS COULD EXTEND AS FAR E AS WRN OH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT CONTINUES AT LEAST ANOTHER COUPLE OF HOURS /THRU 08-10Z/...PRIMARILY ACROSS PARTS OF SOUTHEASTERN ARKANSAS INTO NORTHWEST MISSISSIPPI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: VIGOROUS CONVECTION...INCLUDING DISCRETE SUPERCELLULAR STORMS... PERSISTS IN A NARROW BROKEN LINE...WITHIN A LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENT ZONE NOW EXTENDING ACROSS NORTHWESTERN LOUISIANA INTO SOUTHEASTERN ARKANSAS. THIS IS OCCURRING NEAR THE SHARP SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCING COLD FRONT...WHICH MAY ALREADY BE UNDERCUTTING THE SOUTHERNMOST CELLS TO THE SOUTH AND EAST OF SHREVEPORT. AN INTENSE CELL CROSSING THE LOUISIANA/ARKANSAS BORDER AREA MAY STILL BE SUPPORTED BY INFLOW EMANATING FROM AN UNSTABLE PRE-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT...BUT THIS MAY BEGIN TO BECOME CUT-OFF AS THE STORM CONTINUES NORTHEASTWARD THROUGH AREAS NEAR/EAST OF MONTICELLO AR AND NORTHWEST OF GREENVILLE MS BETWEEN NOW AND 09-10Z. INFLUENCE OF LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION ASSOCIATED WITH AN IMPULSE LIFTING TO THE WEST/NORTHWEST OF THE REGION APPEARS LIKELY TO BEGIN TO DECREASE DURING THIS TIME...AND SOUTHERLY 850 MB FLOW MAY BEGIN TO WEAKEN SOME...RESULTING IN DIMINISHING SHEAR. UNTIL THEN...THOUGH... CONVECTION MAY REMAIN CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WIND GUSTS OR AN ISOLATED TORNADO. ..KERR.. 01/13/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL APPEARS TO BE DIMINISHING. THE REMAINING VALID PORTION OF WW 4 MAY BE CANCELLED EARLY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SHARP SURFACE FRONTAL ZONE CONTINUES A SLOW SOUTHWARD ADVANCEMENT ACROSS THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY/WESTERN GULF COAST REGION. THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE RECENT NEW CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN OCCURRING IN A POST-FRONTAL WARM ADVECTION REGIME ACROSS PARTS OF EASTERN TEXAS...WHERE A MOIST SOUTHERLY INFLOW OF GULF MOISTURE CONTINUES ABOVE A SHALLOW...BUT DEEPENING SURFACE BASED STABLE LAYER. GIVEN CAPE EVIDENT IN RAPID REFRESH FORECAST SOUNDINGS...SOME HAIL MAY NOT BE COMPLETELY OUT OF THE QUESTION WITH THESE STORMS...BUT THIS POTENTIAL SEEMS LIKELY TO DIMINISH THROUGH 11-12Z...AS THE COLD SURFACE-BASED LAYER CONTINUES TO DEEPEN ACROSS THE SABINE VALLEY AND TEXAS COASTAL PLAIN. OTHERWISE...WITH THE MOST PROMINENT FRONTAL WAVE NOW DEVELOPING ACROSS THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY INTO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION...POTENTIAL FOR STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER BASED STORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY APPEARS LOW THROUGH AT LEAST MID TO LATE MORNING. ..KERR.. 01/13/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
